business.title: Photocrosslinked gelatin hydrogel-mediated IGF-1 delivery promotes early cartilage-like tissue formation in a rabbit auricular defect model
business.description: Auricular cartilage has a limited capacity for self-repair. Insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) promotes chondrocyte proliferation and extracellular matrix synthesis; however, its therapeutic efficacy is constrained by rapid diffusion and a short in vivo half-life. In this study, we investigated whether IGF-1 delivered in a previously developed visible-light photocrosslinked gelatin hydrogel could promote cartilage repair. In a mouse subcutaneous model, ex vivo fluorescence imaging over 14 days showed that the hydrogel prolonged the local retention of fluorescently labeled IGF-1 compared with IGF-1 solution. In a rabbit auricular-cartilage defect model, defects were treated with saline, IGF-1 solution, hydrogel alone, or IGF-1-loaded hydrogel (n = 5 per group) and evaluated 1 month later. The IGF-1-loaded hydrogel group formed cartilage-like tissue with rounded cells within lacunae, proteoglycan-rich matrix, and type-II collagen, which occupied 83.8% of the defect length compared with 6.4% in the hydrogel-only group. This group also showed higher COL2A1, ACAN, SOX9, and COL1A1 expression, more Ki-67-positive cells, and increased peripheral angiogenesis, without calcification. IGF-1 delivery using photocrosslinked gelatin hydrogels, which prolonged local IGF-1 retention, is thus a promising strategy for promoting early cartilage-like tissue formation, although long-term maturation and mechanical function remain to be established.

science.title: A chromosome-level genome assembly and developmental transcriptome of the facultative parasitic nematode Pelodera strongyloides
science.description: Pelodera strongyloides is a free-living-preferring facultative parasitic nematode belonging to the family Rhabditidae and closely related to Caenorhabditis elegans. Its intermediate evolutionary position during the transition to parasitism, combined with a short life cycle and gonochoristic reproduction, makes it an attractive model for studying the origins of nematode parasitism. Here, we present a chromosome-level genome assembly and a multi-stage transcriptomic dataset for a P. strongyloides isolate from Guangzhou. The 177.6 Mb genome was assembled into 11 chromosomes (scaffold N50 = 15.16 Mb) using PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing, Illumina short-read polishing, and Hi-C chromatin conformation capture, and was annotated with 16,767 protein-coding genes. We also generated RNA-seq data spanning seven developmental stages from egg to adult. This integrated genomic and transcriptomic resource provides a foundation for comparative evolutionary studies aimed at identifying genes involved in nematode parasitism.
